newsitem.title: UK: LME copper off lows after big stock decline.
newsitem.headline: LME copper off lows after big stock decline.

text.p: Copper prices quickly recovered from a dip below $2,000 a tonne early on Tuesday on the London Metal Exchange (LME), boosted by a larger-than-expected drawdown in stocks.
Other base metals came under early pressure in line with the flagship contract, but also stabilised.

"First there was a bit of trade selling, and then quite good trade buying on the back of stocks," said one European dealer. "People were only looking for a stock drawdown of 7,000 to 10,000 tonnes, so the figure was a bit of a surprise."
Far Eastern selling was also seen by traders early on.
By 0958 GMT three month copper futures were quoted at $2,008/12 a tonne, down from Monday's afternoon kerb close of $2,016 but above the low of the morning so far of $1,995.
Stocks fell 13,475 tonnes to a total of just 132,350 tonnes, the lowest for over six years.
"To me it's a miracle this market isn't any higher. Some positions must still be around from the Sumitomo scandal," a trader said.
Near term support was pegged at $1,990 then $1,970, with resistance pegged at $2,040 thne $2,070.
Aluminium dipped early on before recovering with copper.
Three month futures were last indicated at $1,410/12 from $1,415.50 after dipping to around $1,407 in early dealings. Stocks fell 225 tonnes, in line with market expectations.
Nickel surrendered some of Monday's fund-driven gains, slipping to $7,360/80 from $7,409. Stocks rose 108 tonnes.
Fundamentally the market still looked weak, but traders said bullish chart patterns may be enough to lift values again soon.
"The 10-day and 30-day moving averages are heading for a bullish cross probably in a couple of days," said one.
The big target for nickel is pegged at the September peak of $7,820.
Lead edged back to $742/5 from $746 after stocks fell 775 tonnes, while zinc slipped to $1,050/51 from $1,054 after stocks fell 2,275 tonnes.
Tin was little changed at $5,980/90 from $6,000. Stocks rose 20 tonnes.
Alloy was last indicated at $1,260/70 from $1,266. Stocks fell 840 tonnes.
